case_name: Sussex County Planning & Zoning Commission v. Smokey Hollow, LLC

issues.label: Certiorari scope and remedy
issues.why: The court must confirm certiorari is the proper vehicle and define the permissible remedy (e.g., striking conditions vs remand).

issues.label: Jurisdiction over Commission action
issues.why: The court must ensure it has jurisdiction to review the Commission’s subdivision-condition decision.

issues.label: Finality of challenged action
issues.why: The court must determine whether the conditional preliminary-plan approval (and/or reconsideration denial) is a final, reviewable action.

issues.label: Timeliness of the petition
issues.why: The court must verify the certiorari petition was filed within any applicable limitations period.

issues.label: Exhaustion of administrative remedies
issues.why: The court must decide whether Smokey Hollow had to appeal to County Council under § 99-39(A) before seeking certiorari.

issues.label: Effect of reconsideration procedure
issues.why: The court must determine how § 99-39(H) (no appeal from reconsideration decision) affects review and finality.

issues.label: Standing and aggrievement
issues.why: The court must confirm Smokey Hollow is sufficiently aggrieved by the conditions to seek relief.

issues.label: Proper record on certiorari
issues.why: The court must identify what documents/testimony constitute the record and whether review is record-bound.

issues.label: Standard of review articulation
issues.why: The court must apply the correct mix of de novo review for law and substantial-evidence review for fact/discretion.

issues.label: Deference to agency interpretation
issues.why: The court must decide what deference, if any, to give the Commission’s interpretation of County Code provisions.

issues.label: Commission statutory authority
issues.why: The court must determine the Commission’s legal authority under state law and County Code to approve/deny/condition subdivisions.

issues.label: Commission vs Council roles
issues.why: The court must respect the division between Commission’s administrative function and Council’s legislative zoning function.

issues.label: As-of-right GR zoning effect
issues.why: The court must consider how as-of-right residential use in GR constrains the Commission’s conditioning power.

issues.label: Subdivision code compliance duty
issues.why: The court must decide whether the Commission must approve any code-compliant plan, and the limits of conditioning that approval.

issues.label: Source of conditioning power
issues.why: The court must identify the legal basis (e.g., § 99-9(A)) authorizing “specific changes or modifications.”

issues.label: Reasonableness test for conditions
issues.why: The court must define and apply the governing standard for when a subdivision condition is “reasonable.”

issues.label: Nexus to legitimate objectives
issues.why: The court must ensure each condition has a sufficient connection to health/safety/welfare or code purposes, not mere preference.

issues.label: Proportionality of conditions
issues.why: The court must consider whether conditions are proportionate to identified impacts (avoiding overburdening the applicant).

issues.label: Non-arbitrariness and consistency
issues.why: The court must assess whether conditions were imposed consistently with past practice and not arbitrarily.

issues.label: Substantial evidence for factual predicates
issues.why: The court must decide whether the record contains substantial evidence of flooding, wetland encroachment, and access constraints.

issues.label: Reliance on public testimony
issues.why: The court must decide how much weight can be given to neighbor testimony vs technical evidence and whether it is competent evidence.

issues.label: Improper neighborhood veto concern
issues.why: The court must ensure conditions were not imposed merely to appease opposition rather than address legitimate impacts.

issues.label: Findings and explanation adequacy
issues.why: The court must determine whether the Commission must articulate reasons for each condition and whether omissions are legal error.

issues.label: Condition A: authority to delete lot
issues.why: The court must decide whether the Commission can require elimination of a lot rather than impose less intrusive mitigation.

issues.label: Condition A: code conflict analysis
issues.why: The court must determine whether deleting lot 64 conflicts with subdivision regulations that would otherwise allow it.

issues.label: Condition A: wetland crossing/access
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether access requiring crossing wetlands is a permissible basis to deny/condition a lot’s approval.

issues.label: Condition A: flooding/drainage impacts
issues.why: The court must decide whether flooding/runoff risk to Fox Haven supports deleting the lot under applicable standards.

issues.label: Condition A: environmental constraints
issues.why: The court must consider whether wetlands presence makes the lot non-developable under existing environmental/setback rules.

issues.label: Condition A: perimeter setback relevance
issues.why: The court must determine whether the 30-foot perimeter setback is the correct comparator and whether the Commission contradicted it.

issues.label: Condition A: mitigation alternatives
issues.why: The court must consider whether the Commission had to consider reasonable alternatives (e.g., buffers/landscaping) instead of deletion.

issues.label: Condition A: internal consistency
issues.why: The court must assess whether the Commission’s stated reasons align with the actual condition imposed and the site plan.

issues.label: Condition O: buffer vs setback meaning
issues.why: The court must interpret the Code’s distinction between a wetlands “setback” and a wetlands “resource buffer.”

issues.label: Condition O: applicable code version
issues.why: The court must determine which ordinance provisions govern a pending application (timing/vesting).

issues.label: Former §115-25F(3)(a)(4) scope
issues.why: The court must decide whether the former provision regulates only building/paving setbacks or also authorizes land-area buffers.

issues.label: Ordinance 2852 applicability
issues.why: The court must interpret whether Ordinance 2852 applies and, if so, how its requirements operate (average vs fixed).

issues.label: Pending-application exemption effect
issues.why: The court must decide whether Ordinance 2852’s exemption bars imposing its buffer requirements on this application.

issues.label: Commission power to exceed code
issues.why: The court must determine whether the Commission may impose a buffer more stringent than the Code absent express authorization.

issues.label: Condition O: fixed vs average buffer
issues.why: The court must decide whether a fixed 25-foot minimum is consistent with any “average” standard or contradicts it.

issues.label: Condition O: factual support needed
issues.why: The court must assess whether site conditions justify a fixed buffer and whether evidence supports that justification.

issues.label: Condition O: lack of stated reasons
issues.why: The court must decide whether imposing the buffer without explanation is reversible legal error.

issues.label: Cluster development standards relevance
issues.why: The court must determine whether cluster standards apply to this subdivision and could supply buffer authority.

issues.label: Coastal Area environmental assessment
issues.why: The court must confirm whether any Coastal Area environmental assessment requirements affect permissible conditions.

issues.label: PLUS review legal significance
issues.why: The court must decide what weight PLUS comments/approvals carry and whether the Commission may depart from them.

issues.label: Vested rights doctrine
issues.why: The court must decide whether Smokey Hollow had vested rights in prior setback rules upon submission or PLUS completion.

issues.label: Retroactivity of ordinances
issues.why: The court must analyze whether applying new buffer rules would be impermissibly retroactive under County law.

issues.label: Interpretation of defined terms
issues.why: The court must apply Code definitions (e.g., setback, resource buffer, wetlands) to the conditions imposed.

issues.label: Consistency with Comprehensive Plan
issues.why: The court must consider whether the subdivision/conditions must be consistent with the Comprehensive Plan and how that affects review.

issues.label: Procedural due process at hearings
issues.why: The court must ensure the applicant had notice and a fair opportunity to be heard regarding the conditions and evidence.

issues.label: Record support for code “uphold” claim
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether the Commission’s assertion it acted “to uphold the code” is legally and factually substantiated.

issues.label: Severability of conditions
issues.why: The court must decide whether striking conditions affects the remainder of the 19 conditions or the approval’s validity.

issues.label: Proper disposition after error
issues.why: The court must choose between striking the conditions, remanding for findings, or allowing reimposition with adequate support.

issues.label: Burden of proof allocation
issues.why: The court must determine who bears the burden to show unreasonableness/legal error on certiorari.

issues.label: Substantial evidence vs speculation
issues.why: The court must distinguish competent evidence of flooding/wetlands impacts from speculation or generalized concerns.

issues.label: Equal treatment/consistency concerns
issues.why: The court must consider whether imposing atypical buffers/loss of lots raises issues of inconsistent treatment under the Code.

issues.label: Police power limits
issues.why: The court must ensure conditions serve legitimate police-power ends and do not exceed delegated authority.

issues.label: Takings/exactions implications
issues.why: The court must consider whether forced loss of buildable lots or fixed buffers could constitute an unconstitutional exaction or taking (if raised/implicit).

issues.label: Scope of issues preserved
issues.why: The court must determine which arguments were preserved before the Commission/Council and are properly before the court.
